meta_description_en: A guide to using the DU52P3 disc formatting tool for ZX Spectrum +3, including format options, menu navigation, and customization.
meta_description_ru: Руководство по использованию утилиты форматирования дисков DU52P3 для ZX Spectrum +3, включая описание форматов и настройку.
body_en_plain:
DU Formatter v5.02 for +3DOS
    J. Elliott, 8 July 1994.
  ============================

The next program, the DU52P3
formatter, is a menu-driven disc
formatter for Spectrum +3 compu-
ters. Features of DU52P3 are:

* 15 different formats;

* CP/M and DOS discs can be for-
matted;


* Discs can be initialised for
timestamping(not used by +3DOS,
only by CP/M)

* Disc names can be specified
(not used by +3DOS,only by CP/M)

* Disc drives can be set to acc-
ept fixed formats - for example,
formats which +3DOS does not au-
tomatically recognise.

* Disc boot sectors can be sav-
ed as files.

To use DU52P3, type the command:

LOAD "DU52P3"

The DU52P3 main screen will
then appear.


The menu system is designed to
be familiar to those who have
used the +3 menu system. A high-
lighted bar will appear over a
list of options, and it can be
moved with the up and down cur-
sor keys. There are two option
types:


Command options - Move the bar
over the option and press ENTER
to execute.

Input options - recognisable by
the flashing cursor which app-
ears in the menu bar. Type the
input and press ENTER after-
wards. To abandon the input move
the bar off the option using the
cursor keys.


When the menu bar is over a
Command option, shortcut keys
are effective. These make the
bar jump to a particular opti-
on. For example, in the format
selection menu, the shortcut
keys are shown on the left-hand
side. Often the shortcut for an
option is its first letter.


The screen has three lines at
the top in reverse video:

The top line holds general inf-
ormation about the state of the
drives. A "Fixed Format" drive
can only recognise discs of one
format; an "Auto Select" drive
can recognise more than one
type.


If a drive name appears after
the message"Using" then the disc
shouldn't be taken out of the
drive. The lower two lines hold
information specific to a parti-
cular activity. This might be a
list of valid keypresses or inf-
ormation about what the computer
is doing.

When the main screen appears,
there are four options:


1=Select Disc Type

2=Format Disc

3=Save Boot Sector to File

BREAK=Exit.


       1=Select Disc Type
       ------------------
You will be asked which drive
to use; then whether it should
be "auto selecting" or "fixed
format". The main reasons for
using a fixed format are:

(i) To use a format (eg 792k
format) which +3DOS can't read
automatically;

(ii) To use a +3DOS sector
editor (eg Disk Doctor) on a
DOS disc;

(iii) Option 3 (Save Boot
Sector) needs to use a fixed
format. If you chose "fixed
format" you will then be shown
a menu of all possible formats.


If you choose a DOS format, you
will actually be given a fixed
+3DOS format which is close
enough to the DOS format to
allow the use of sector editors
etc.


If, from this menu, you choose
a 40-track format, you may then
be asked about a"format option".
This will be "Single track" 99%
of the time; "Double track" has
been included mainly for histor-
ical reasons - see "Double Track
Discs" later.







         2=Format Disc
         -------------
You will be asked which drive to
use; then which format. If you
choose a 40-track format,you may
then be asked: Single or Double
Track. If a drive can read 720k
discs,it is Double Track; other-
wise it is Single.

Then, insert the disc and wait.
After the main part of formatt-
ing is complete,you may be asked
whether the disc should be init-
ialised for date-stamping. Only
CP/M and +3DOS support date-
stamped discs (and +3DOS doesn't
actually set the date or time).
Note that if you select this op-
tion, you will still need to use
the CP/M utility SET to turn on
datestamping.

Finally,you will be asked wheth-
er the disc should have a label.
Labels are used in LocoScript,
and appear in DOS directory
listings. They are also used by
some PD disc cataloguing prog-
rams.

Discs formatted by DU52P3 cannot
be used to boot CP/M or DOS.


       3=Save Boot Sector
       ------------------

You should have set the drive
whose boot sector you want to
save, to the correct fixed form-
at. The computer will read the
boot sector and save it as a
conventional file.


            Formats
            -------
It is not possible to supply a
version of DU52P3 that makes
auto-booting discs, due to the
fact that different computers
use the same format but differ-
ent boot sectors. However, if
you have CP/M, you can use the
CP/M programs DU52 and DU52CON
to copy the boot sectors from
your start-of-day disc into the
program DU52P3, so that DU52P3
will make auto-booting discs.

Supplied formats are:

1. PCW 8256 CF2:As made by DISC-
KIT, f2=Disc, +3DOS FORMAT etc.
You can't boot from them but see
DU52CON below).


2. CPC System:Only really of use
for a CPC.

3. CPC Data: You get 178k per
side rather than 173k, with no
catches, but you can't boot from
them under any circumstances.

4. IBM Format: 8 sectors per
track instead of 9. If you form-
at a 5" disc in this format, you
may be able to read it on a PC
running DOS Plus.

5. Large directory CF2: You get
192 directory entries instead of
64, in case you want to store a
lot of 1k files.

6. Standard XCF2: You get 192k
per disc instead of 173k, and 96
directory entries.

7. Large Directory XCF2: You get
189k per disc, and 192 directory
entries.

8. XCF2 with no system track:You
get 198k per disc, but the disc
will not auto-detect so you have
to use "fixed format".

9. PCW 9000 CF2DD: Standard 706k
disc. Can be copied by DISCKIT,
f2=Disc etc. If you use DU52CON,
you will be able to boot from
these discs.

A. QUAD:with no system track and
a small directory. Very similar
to CF2DD, but there is 716k per
disc, not 706k, and only 128
directory entries. The disc will
not auto-detect.


B. XCF2DD:You get 784k per disc,
in blocks of 4k.

C. XCF2DD: with no system track
You get 792k per disc, but it
won't auto-detect.

D. XCF2DD: with no system track
and a small directory. You get
796k per disc but it won't auto-
detect and there are only 128
directory entries.

E. DOS standard. Usable under
MSDOS, PCDOS, DRDOS and Novell
DOS. 713k per disc, and 128
entries in the root directory.
The boot sector supplied is the
non-booting "msdisc" sector by G
Mortreuil.



F. DOS Oddball: The program
MSODBALL.COM can convert this
DOS format to and from format 9,
preserving all files. The boot
sector supplied is the non-
booting "msodball" sector by G
Mortreuil.



       Double Track Discs
       ------------------
Discs made in 3.5" drives, the
B: drive of a PCW 8512, either
drive of a PCW 9512 or an
external 720k disc drive are
referred to as "Double Track".
These discs cannot be read in
"Single Track" drives, such as
the A: drive of a PCW 8256, a
CPC 6128 or a Spectrum +3.


There are therefore two types of
173k disc; those made in "Single
Track" drives(the usual sort)and
those made in "Double Track"
drives by this program or the
original DU49(on which this pro-
gram is based). The two are not
interchangeable.The "Format Opt-
ion" menu allows "Double Track"
drives to read both types of
disc but"Single Track"drives can
only read "Single Track" discs.

   Format Editor DU52CON.COM:
   --------------------------
The format editor is a CP/M pro-
gram which can give DU52P3 new
formats or add or replace boot
sectors. It is not provided with
DU52P3, but should be available
as part of the DU52 package from
PD libraries.

Here is a worked example of
changing a boot sector for +3
CP/M:

1. In CP/M, run DU52.COM.

2. Select option 1. Choose
"Fixed Format", "PCW 8256 CF2",
"Single Track"

3. Select option 3. Insert your
CP/M Start of Day disc, and
follow the instructions, saving
the boot sector as C:BOOTCPM.BIN

4. Leave DU52, and run DU52CON.

5. Load a copy of DU52P3.HED

6. Select option B. Choose "PCW
8256 CF2".


7. Enter the filename:
   C:BOOTCPM.BIN


8. Save DU52P3 as DU52P3.BIN.


9. Reset the computer, insert
the disc with DU52P3.BIN and
type:


COPY "DU52P3.BIN" TO SPECTRUM
FORMAT


Subsequently, all discs form-
atted by the new version of
DU52P3 in the appropriate format
will be able to boot CP/M.



  Editing DU52P3.HED manually:


All the addresses in DU52P3.HED
are given as though it was load-
ed at address 256. Therefore, if
you load the file at for example
33024,you will have to add 32768
to each address to make it acc-
urate. Similarly, when changing
addresses, you will have to sub-
tract the same figure from the
real address.


In the following information,
LOADADD is the address that
DU52P3 was loaded at...



The configuration data are loca-
ted at LOADADD+3 - LOADADD+13:

LOADADD+3:DEFB52H:Version number
- v5.02. Used by DU52CON to
check for a correct DU52.COM.

LOADADD+4:DEFWFLAGS:The address
of a 15-byte flags area relative
to 256.

LOADADD+6:DEFWMENU: The address
of the formats menu (relative to
256).

LOADADD+8:DEFWXDPBS:The address
of the XDPBs for the fixed for-
mats (relative to 256).

LOADADD+10:DEFWSECTORS:The addr-
ess of the bootsectors table
(relative ;to 256).

LOADADD+12:DEFWENDPRG:Length of
the CODE file + 256. If more
boot sectors or patches are
added to the end of the file,
this value should be changed.



             FLAGS:

Each byte corresponds to one of
the formats in the menu - so
FLAGS+0 is for format 1, FLAGS+1
is for format 2 etc. Each byte
should have:

Bit 0: Set to 0 if the formatter
should generate a boot sector
for the format. Set to 1 if the
formatter should use a ready-
made boot sector.


Bit 1 : Set to 0 if the format
is a CP/M format. Set to 1 if
the format is a DOS format.

Bit 2 : Set to 0 if the boot
information is not to be written
to the directory. Set to 1 if
the boot information is to be
written to the directory.

Bits 3-7: Reserved (set to 0).



MENU:DEFBrow,column,width_of_
           options,no_of_options

DEFBheading

DEFBmenu_entry,shortcut,0,0;15
times


The MENU is a data structure
containing the list of formats.
The first four bytes should not
be altered, unless you wish to
reduce the number of options by
changing the byte at MENU+3. The
heading is 60 bytes long, and is
printed at the top of the menu.
Each entry is 60 bytes long, and
is followed by its shortcut
character (1 byte) and then two
zeroes, which must not be
altered.

XDPBS:

Each XDPB is a standard Amstrad
XDPB, 27 bytes long. The last
byte should be set to 0FFh. The
XDPBs follow one after the
other.


SECTORS:

DEFWsector_for_format_1

DEFWsector_for_format_2 etc.

Each entry in the table is the
address of a boot sector (relat-
ive to 256). If a format's entry
in the flags table has bit 0 set
the corresponding boot sector
will be written to disc as the
first sector on the first reser-
ved track. If the address is 0,
then load the boot sector at
(LOADADD+ENDPRG-256), change the
corresponding entry accordingly,
and add 512 to ENDPRG.

PRESS N NOW TO LOAD DU FORMATTER
.
body_en:
## DU Formatter v5.02 for +3DOS
**J. Elliott, 8 July 1994.**

The DU52P3 formatter is a menu-driven disc formatter for Spectrum +3 computers. Features include 15 different formats, support for CP/M and DOS discs, timestamping/labelling support, fixed format selection, and saving boot sectors to files.

### Usage
Type `LOAD "DU52P3"` to start the program. The menu system is similar to the +3 standard: use arrow keys to navigate and `ENTER` to select. Command options execute immediately, while Input options require typed data followed by `ENTER`.

### Main Menu
1. **Select Disc Type**: Choose drive and format (Auto Select or Fixed). Fixed formats are essential for non-standard formats (e.g., 792k) or sector editors.
2. **Format Disc**: Performs formatting. You may be prompted for "Single" or "Double" track depending on the drive capabilities.
3. **Save Boot Sector to File**: Reads and saves the boot sector as a file.
`BREAK` to exit.

### Supported Formats
The utility supports various formats including PCW, CPC, IBM, and XCF2. Note that auto-booting discs require specific boot sectors; use the `DU52CON` utility to patch them.

### Customization
`DU52CON.COM` is a CP/M program that allows you to add or replace boot sectors and manage new formats. Detailed internal structure (FLAGS, MENU, XDPBS, SECTORS) is provided for advanced users to edit `DU52P3.HED` manually.
body_ru:
## DU Formatter v5.02 для +3DOS
**J. Elliott, 8 июля 1994 г.**

DU52P3 — это меню-ориентированная утилита для форматирования дисков на ZX Spectrum +3. Основные возможности: 15 различных форматов, поддержка дисков CP/M и DOS, использование меток времени и имен дисков, настройка на фиксированные форматы, а также сохранение загрузочных секторов в файлы.

### Использование
Введите `LOAD "DU52P3"` для запуска программы. Система меню привычна пользователям +3: навигация стрелками, выбор через `ENTER`. Командные опции выполняются сразу, вводимые данные подтверждаются клавишей `ENTER`.

### Главное меню
1. **Выбор типа диска**: Выбор дисковода и формата (автоопределение или фиксированный). Фиксированный формат необходим для нестандартных форматов (например, 792к) или работы с редакторами секторов.
2. **Форматирование**: Основная операция. В зависимости от типа дисковода может потребоваться выбор между "Single" (одинарная) и "Double" (двойная) дорожкой.
3. **Сохранить загрузочный сектор**: Считывание и сохранение загрузочного сектора в файл.
`BREAK` для выхода.

### Поддерживаемые форматы
Утилита поддерживает форматы PCW, CPC, IBM и XCF2. Обратите внимание: для создания загрузочных дисков требуются специфические загрузочные секторы. Используйте утилиту `DU52CON` для их интеграции.

### Настройка
`DU52CON.COM` — это CP/M-программа, позволяющая добавлять новые форматы и менять загрузочные секторы. Для опытных пользователей приведено описание внутренней структуры файла `DU52P3.HED` (FLAGS, MENU, XDPBS, SECTORS) для внесения ручных правок.
